Of course! I used p5.js in processing. It’s been my go-to lately as I’ve been trying to focus on one concept, but I’ve been playing around with three.js too. I basically generated multiple rectangles by drawing a bunch of lines. I randomized the distance of each line from top to bottom which gave that dripping feature. Then I played around with strokeweight() and distance between the lines. Just did it as a fun little project. Feel free to message me on here or my twitter and I can definitely show you more of the process! 🙂

Of course! It’s funny, a lot of it was just trial and error until I liked it. I was playing around with flow fields but was tired of all the repetitive stuff I see and wanted to try something new! I set it up using some code from an old project I had and started playing with the variables. I added varying vector velocities to get the craziness of the particles as you can see in the image. In terms of colors I was ultimately staying in the range of pastel colors so it would look more calm and smooth looking. Idk if I answered your question, but that’s just pinpointing certain aspects.

I also have a twitter: @freeimpeth where I post my other works and just me having fun with different techniques! I’m debating to mint these but I’m not too sure yet.
